instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The application reads the password of an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database from a configuration file on each instance. A new security rule requires that the password is rotated automatically every 30 days without a new deployment of the application. Minimal code changes are acceptable. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the password as a SecureString parameter in Parameter Store, turn on automatic rotation for the parameter, and read it at run time.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager, turn on automatic rotation, and change the application to read the secret at run time through a cache.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager, turn on automatic rotation, and pass the current value to each instance as user data at launch.

options.label: D
options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command every 30 days to change the database password, write it into the file on each instance, and restart the application.

items.stem: A company stores the ID of its approved Amazon Machine Image (AMI) as a standard String parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Launch templates for several applications read the parameter. The security team wants to be notified when nobody has updated the parameter for 90 days, so that the team reviews the image. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that reads the parameter history every day and notifies the security team through Amazon SNS.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep the parameter in the standard tier, attach an Expiration policy for 90 days, and notify the security team when the parameter expires.

options.label: C
options.text: Change the parameter to the advanced tier, attach a NoChangeNotification policy, and create an Amazon EventBridge rule that notifies the security team.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the parameter in the standard tier, attach a NoChangeNotification policy, and create an Amazon EventBridge rule that notifies the security team.

items.stem: A company runs an internet-facing application behind an Application Load Balancer. The HTTPS listener currently uses a certificate for one domain name from a third-party certificate authority (CA) that the company imported into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). The certificate expires next month. A contract requires the company to keep the same CA. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Change the validation method of the imported certificate to DNS validation, and add the CNAME record so that ACM renews it.

options.label: B
options.text: Get the renewed certificate from the CA, upload it to IAM, and change the listener to use the IAM certificate instead of the ACM one.

options.label: C
options.text: Get the renewed certificate from the CA, and reimport it into ACM to the ARN of the existing certificate before the expiration date.

options.label: D
options.text: Wait for ACM managed renewal, which renews the imported certificate and deploys it to the listener before the expiration date.

items.stem: A company stores a database secret in AWS Secrets Manager in account A. The secret is encrypted with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager. An AWS Lambda function in account B must read the secret. The IAM role of the function already allows secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret and kms:Decrypt on KMS keys in account A. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST securely? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Change the KMS key of the secret to a customer managed key whose key policy allows the IAM role of the function in account B to decrypt.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach a resource-based policy to the secret that allows all principals in account B to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.

options.label: C
options.text: Keep the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager, and add kms:Decrypt for account B to the resource-based policy of the secret.

options.label: D
options.text: Add the IAM role of the function in account B to the key policy of the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager in account A.

options.label: E
options.text: Attach a resource-based policy to the secret that allows the IAM role of the function in account B to call secretsmanager:GetSecretValue.

items.stem: A company hosts an internet-facing web application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Scaling events replace the instances often. The company's domain is hosted in Amazon Route 53. Clients on the internet must connect over HTTPS so that data is encrypted in transit. The certificate for the domain must renew automatically. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Request a public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) with DNS validation, and add it to an HTTPS listener on the load balancer.

options.label: B
options.text: Request a public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), and install it with its private key in the web server software on each instance.

options.label: C
options.text: Issue an exportable public certificate in ACM, and run a script on each instance that installs the certificate after every renewal.

options.label: D
options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer with TCP pass-through, and install self-signed certificates in the web server software on each instance.

items.stem: A company runs an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in private subnets of a VPC. A custom AWS Lambda rotation function for an AWS Secrets Manager secret runs in the same private subnets so that it can reach the database. The subnets have no route to the internet, and every rotation fails because the function cannot reach Secrets Manager. The security team prefers private connectivity to AWS services. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?

options.label: A
options.text: Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet, and add a default route to the NAT gateway in the route tables of the private subnets.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in the VPC, and allow HTTPS from the security group of the function to the endpoint.

options.label: C
options.text: Move the rotation function out of the VPC, and let it call the public Secrets Manager endpoint over the internet.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager, and add the endpoint route to the route tables of the private subnets.

items.stem: An administrator deleted a secret in AWS Secrets Manager from the console yesterday and kept the default settings. The application that uses the secret now fails to connect to its Amazon RDS database. The IAM policies of the application name the ARN of the secret. The company needs the application to work again as soon as possible. What should a solutions architect do?

options.label: A
options.text: Open an AWS Support case, and ask AWS to recover the deleted secret from its internal storage.

options.label: B
options.text: Read the AWSPREVIOUS version of the deleted secret, and store that value in the configuration of the application.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new secret with the same name and the same value, and update the application to read the new secret.

options.label: D
options.text: Restore the deleted secret in Secrets Manager, because the deletion is still inside its recovery window.

items.stem: A company runs an application in us-east-1 and keeps a warm standby copy in a second Region, us-west-2. The application reads its database credentials from a secret in AWS Secrets Manager in us-east-1, and the secret is rotated every 30 days. If us-east-1 fails, the standby application must still read the current credentials in us-west-2. The design must stay resilient, with rotation managed in one place. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Run a scheduled AWS Lambda function in us-west-2 that copies the secret value from us-east-1 into a separate secret after each rotation.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the credentials as an advanced SecureString parameter in us-east-1, and share the parameter with us-west-2 through AWS RAM.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the standby application in us-west-2 to call the Secrets Manager endpoint in us-east-1 to read the secret.

options.label: D
options.text: Replicate the secret to us-west-2, and promote the replica secret to a standalone secret if us-east-1 becomes unavailable.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently keeps one value in its source code. The value is a database password that company policy requires to be rotated automatically every 30 days. The company wants to move the value out of the code and read it at run time through the AWS SDK. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the value as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager, and turn on automatic rotation.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the value as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypt it with a new customer managed KMS key, and turn on automatic rotation.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the value as an advanced SecureString parameter in Parameter Store, and attach a NoChangeNotification policy to the parameter.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the value as a standard String parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and change the parameter value when required.

items.stem: A company runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer in the eu-west-1 Region. The load balancer has an HTTPS listener with a public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for app.example.com. Users around the world report slow page loads, so the company adds an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the load balancer. Viewers must reach the distribution at app.example.com, and data must stay encrypted in transit. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Copy the existing ACM certificate from the eu-west-1 Region to the US East (N. Virginia) Region, and associate the copy with the distribution.

options.label: B
options.text: Buy a certificate from a third-party certificate authority, import it into ACM in US East (N. Virginia), and associate it with the distribution.

options.label: C
options.text: Request a public certificate for app.example.com in ACM in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, and associate it with the distribution.

options.label: D
options.text: Select the existing ACM certificate from the eu-west-1 Region in the distribution settings, and keep it on the load balancer as well.

items.stem: A company hosts its public domain in Amazon Route 53 and serves its main website from an Application Load Balancer. The company requests a public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) for the load balancer. The operations team wants ACM to renew the certificate automatically, with no action from a person at renewal time. How should the company validate the domain for this certificate?

options.label: A
options.text: Choose email validation, and approve the validation email that ACM sends to the administrative addresses of the domain.

options.label: B
options.text: Import a certificate from a third-party certificate authority into ACM instead of requesting a public ACM certificate.

options.label: C
options.text: Choose HTTP validation, and configure the load balancer to answer the validation requests that ACM sends.

options.label: D
options.text: Choose DNS validation, and add the CNAME record that ACM provides to the hosted zone in Route 53.

items.stem: A company runs internal microservices in several AWS accounts. To isolate its public key infrastructure, the company runs a private certificate authority (CA) in AWS Private CA in a separate security account and shares the CA with the workload accounts. Every client service trusts this CA. In one workload account, client services call an internal Application Load Balancer, and the traffic must be encrypted in transit. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Request a private certificate in ACM from the shared private CA, export it, and install it with its private key in the web server software on each target.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a new private CA in the workload account, request a private certificate in ACM from the new CA, and add it to an HTTPS listener on the load balancer.

options.label: C
options.text: Issue a certificate from the shared private CA with the IssueCertificate API, import it into ACM, and add it to an HTTPS listener on the internal load balancer.

options.label: D
options.text: Request a private certificate in ACM from the shared private CA, and add the certificate to an HTTPS listener on the internal load balancer.

items.stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application currently keeps one value in its source code. The value is an application endpoint URL that the team updates by hand a few times each year. The company wants to move the value out of the code and read it at run time through the AWS SDK. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.label: A
options.text: Store the value as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypt it with a new customer managed KMS key, and turn on automatic rotation.

options.label: B
options.text: Store the value as an advanced SecureString parameter in Parameter Store, and attach a NoChangeNotification policy to the parameter.

options.label: C
options.text: Store the value as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager with the AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager, and turn on automatic rotation.

options.label: D
options.text: Store the value as a standard String parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and change the parameter value when required.
